feedback: Strong exploration — but it ran against origin/v2@9503325, ten commits behind. Since then (now on main): the vm-pool wire protocol gained request/response correlation (drop the proposed vm.rs demux — superseded at a better layer), Scout::dispatch is already concurrent (&self + per-dispatch event subscriptions), and the HTTP API + bounded dispatch loop exist in run.rs. Still valid and wanted: run_now cap-bypass semantics (works in Pause, refused in Stop), preemption with the choose_victim policy (orchestrator runs only, lowest priority, most-recent tiebreak), cancel(session_id, reason), and reconcile_stale_sessions. Re-scout against current main, scoped to: admission control integrated with run.rs dispatch loop + POST /tasks/{id}/run-now endpoint.

Approved. Verified against main: specs has no status/feedback columns so the join is collision-free; render_prompt(task) at scout.rs:362 with the ## Your job splice point at 367; reset_dispatch_attempts, spec_from_row, SpecQueueStatus::as_str all exist as described. Edge cases are decided rather than deferred (most-recent-only with rationale, fence-length escaping, rowid tiebreak, blank feedback, verdict-only statuses). The new echo-prompt-agent.sh fixture plus the parse_complexity ordering trap make the acceptance criterion directly assertable in the no-mock harness.

Approved. Verified against main: SSE_KEEPALIVE=15s and the lag warning in server.rs, EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY=1024 in vm-pool/client, the current SCOUT_AGENT_CMD in images/scout/Dockerfile, and the six sibling from_str impls in models.rs. The cited docs/clients.md section Event volume is indeed absent — good catch on the dangling reference, and writing it is correctly in scope. Storage choice is argued rather than asserted (indexed range scan on the PK matches the ?since= read shape; cascade gives lifetime for free), caps are stated as the issue required (32 KiB/line, 8 MiB/session, head-retention over ring eviction, with rationale), and the two subtle correctness points — paging the SSE replay to completion rather than one limit-sized page, and subscribing before the backfill read — are exactly right and have named regression tests. Accepting the +1 clippy warning (TranscriptStream::from_str) since it matches the six siblings; I will flag the delta in the PR body rather than silence one enum differently. Noting for the operator: the Dockerfile change means transcripts do not actually flow until the scout image is rebuilt.

Approved. Verified against main: PoolConfig::default() vm_timeout=7200 with the reaper at pool/src/lib.rs:585, DISPATCHER private at run.rs:70 (so the pub(crate) change is real), parse_env/record_outcome/is_disconnect/SHUTDOWN_GRACE all as described, dispatch_harness_with_agent at tests/run.rs:409, and the cancelling-means-deallocating module doc at run.rs:20. The default is argued rather than picked: 3600s sits deliberately below vm-pool own 7200s reaper so the app deadline fires first and the diagnostic is ours, with the correct warning that raising one requires raising the other. Routing expiry through ScoutError so record_dispatch_failure and the 3-strike rejection apply unchanged is the right seam. Two honest limitations stated rather than hidden: the budget covers allocation but allocation itself is still unbounded, and the racy task-back-to-New assertion is correctly replaced by an event-log assertion (agreed — do not fix that back into a row read). Minor imprecision, not blocking: finalize_failed takes a reason String from its callers rather than formatting internally, so the timeout branch must pass format!("{e}") itself to get the Display text into exit_reason.

Approved. The central design call is correct and well argued: filter after the fetch in poll_once, never as a labels: argument on the GraphQL query, because Store::reconcile_closed_issues infers upstream closure from absence and its doc comment explicitly requires a complete open set. Verified against main — that contract is documented as described, open_numbers is computed at run.rs:362 before the upsert loop, and labels(first: 20) at github.rs:94 is real. Good catch that the label page size is a latent bug the filter promotes to a real one: an issue with 21+ labels would silently never be ingested. Edge cases are decided with reasons, and the two rejected alternatives for a de-labelled task (writing gh_state=closed, or state=rejected) are rejected on the right grounds — both would persist a label-derived fact or let the poller overwrite Tasks-owned state. Keep the mutation-verified assertion in a_task_whose_issue_loses_the_label_is_kept_and_left_alone; it is the regression guard for the whole design. Also correct to state plainly that this saves no API cost.

Approved (reviewing as Nate's delegate — he green-lit starting the builder). The architecture honors every load-bearing rule: barrier as a deserialization error via the role-tagged union, bundle egress keeping credentials out of VMs, server-side PR creation as the only GitHub write, pr_number-as-identifier with PR state deliberately unqueried. Rebase notes for implementation against current main (the scout ran pre-lifecycle-rename): (1) migration is 0007 now, not 0004; (2) state vocabulary — the spec's 'queued' is today's ready_to_build, so builds consume ready_to_build tasks, TaskState::Building slots between ready_to_build and done, and a failed build returns tasks to ready_to_build (returning to today's queued would re-scout work that has a good spec — the exact mistake the spec itself warns about under the old name); (3) the role-union wire change means the scout image must be rebuilt alongside builder:v1 before the next live scout run.

Send-back from the orchestrator (Nate delegated this verdict). Four things to fix; the first is the big one.

1. Reconcile with open PR #785, do not rebuild it. This spec treats issue #763's fixtures work as hypothetical ("fixtures/ does not exist in this tree"), but it is an open PR right now. Both create fixtures/ at the repo root, crates/tasks/tests/wire_fixtures.rs, a hand-written TasksTests target in app/Tasks.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj plus a Testables scheme entry, both make TasksClient.makeDecoder() non-private, and both add .built to SpecQueueStatus. Two hand-edited pbxproj object graphs will not merge cleanly. Pick one path explicitly: either build on #785 (adding only builds_list.json and velocity.json to its existing generator), or state that #785 is superseded and this change carries the whole harness. Note #785 is currently broken against main -- its Build/BuildDetail types collide with main's BuildItem, which this spec also redefines -- so superseding it is a legitimate option.

2. Renumber the migration. 0009_events_timestamp_idx.sql collides with 0009_orchestrator_watermark.sql, which landed on main in #800 while this scout was running. Duplicate version 9 is a startup failure, not a warning. Use 0010 and re-verify the migration applies over a database that already has 0009.

3. Fix the shipped-work claim. The Notes say 'if a future reader wants shipped-work-only, pull_requests_opened is already that number.' It is not -- a PR opened is not a PR merged, and three PRs are open right now with one that does not compile. Nothing on the wire counts merges. Either drop the sentence or add an honest merged count; do not ship a doc line that teaches the next reader to read opened-PRs as shipped work.

4. Cut or defer /velocity. It is the most expensive part of this change (endpoint, model, migration, index, fixture, three tests) and the least valuable block on a project with 32 lifetime ingests and two completed builds -- the KPI row reads mostly zeros over any 7-day window. The index is justified by 'a full scan once per connected client per event' against an events table under 200 rows. Land In flight, Needs you, and Recent PRs first; bring velocity back when there is enough history for the numbers to mean something. If you keep it, justify it against the actual data volume rather than the general principle.

Keep as-is: the read-only Home surface, the client-side waitingSince join, the chrono to_rfc3339 '+00:00' vs 'Z' cutoff pitfall, and the deliberate absence of ORDER BY in the velocity query. Those are correct and well-argued.

Also flag for whoever picks this up: no Swift was compiled (Linux scout). The macOS build and pbxproj changes are unverified and must be checked with make app / make app-test before this is trusted.
